paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Jesus has the power to heal, and He is also willing. The man with leprosy says, "Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean," and Jesus answers, "I am willing" (Luke 5:12-13). So if you've ever wondered whether Jesus wants to help you, start right there.

Now look at the second man, whose friends carry him, hit a crowd, and refuse to quit. Scripture says, "When Jesus saw their faith," He told the man, "Friend, your sins are forgiven." (Luke 5:20). Jesus goes to the deepest need first, and He does it for a man who came in on a mat. Then He backs up His words by telling him, "get up, pick up your mat, and go home" (Luke 5:24), so everyone can know the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins.

So here's the takeaway, baker. Bring your need to Jesus, and bring the people you love, even if it takes the roof. And notice Jesus Himself, who "frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray" (Luke 5:16). If He made time for that, I think I can stop my oven for a minute too.
